answer: Attention-Duration Gate. An agent earns its vertex only by keeping a persistent work record visible for a fixed window, so each identity must sustain public, checkable activity rather than appear once. The gate admits an identity to the summit of trust only after that record survives continuous review, which forces an attacker to run every fake identity at once. Because the trellis of recorded interactions cannot be compressed or backfilled, scaling to N identities costs roughly N times the sustained attention and compute of one honest agent, paid continuously for the whole window.
